title: Pin resolution policy: affinity rules, rollback tokens, and compatibility windows
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: customers need flexible, predictable semantics for pinning models via tag, semver, or commit hash while also supporting safe rollbacks and runtime selection across Dedicated/Hosted/Private. Existing resolver behaviors are underspecified for: affinity overrides (runtime-tier, region), pinned artifact immutability guarantees, TTLs for resolved pins, and how to represent rollback-able pins in APIs and SDKs.

This ticket defines a cohesive policy for pin resolution precedence, introduces a lightweight rollback token, defines a compatibility window for model binary variants (quantization/compile profile), and outlines API/SDK behavior and telemetry requirements.
background: Engineering has handled pin semantics in multiple ad-hoc places: client-side SDKs attempted to resolve tags locally, the control plane cached resolution with inconsistent TTLs, and runtime fallbacks lacked audit signals. Customers reported surprising rollouts when 'latest' tags changed and difficulties reproducing production behavior when a tag moved. Product asked for a formal policy to enable deterministic rollouts and safe rollbacks, while minimizing runtime latency and preserving cache efficiency.
proposal_summary: 1) Resolution precedence: exact commit hash -> exact semver -> semver range -> explicit tag -> 'latest' default. 2) Introduce 'rollback_token' (opaque ID) returned on successful resolution and stored in audit logs; providing the token to the API/SDK forces that exact resolved artifact regardless of tag movement. 3) Compatibility windows: model onboarding must publish a 'compatibility_profile' string (e.g., 'kv-v2|q4h|cuda-12') and a stability window (e.g., 14 days) indicating when runtime can safely fallback between binary variants of the same model. 4) TTLs and cache staleness: control plane TTLs default to 1 hour, SDKs can opt into 'short_ttl' for development (30s) or 'long_ttl' for high-stability customers (24h). 5) Affinity overrides: requests can include optional affinity headers (region, tier) that influence which compatible variant is selected when multiple artifacts match. 6) Telemetry: every resolution emits events for resolved_id, input_selector, precedence_clause, ttl_used, and rollback_token when applicable.
api_changes:
- Add field 'resolved_rollback_token' to model-resolve response (string).
- Add query param 'force_resolution_token' to generation endpoints to pin exact artifact.
- Add 'compatibility_profile' & 'stability_window_days' to model metadata endpoints.
- Error codes: 409 when selector matches artifacts with incompatible profiles unless 'allow_incompatible=true' is used (opt-in).
- Deprecate client-side tag resolution in favor of control-plane resolution APIs.
sdk_changes:
- SDKs (py/ts/go): remove local tag->artifact resolution logic; call control-plane resolve API.
- Add ModelResolver helper that caches resolution with configurable TTL and exposes a getRollbackToken() helper.
- Expose configuration flags: resolution_ttl, prefer_short_ttl_for_dev, allow_compat_fallback.
- Implement transparent injection of force_resolution_token into requests when user calls resolver.lock() (returns rollback token).
runtime_behavior:
- Runtime selection algorithm: filter artifacts by exact identifier (if provided) -> filter by compatibility_profile match -> apply affinity scoring (region, tier) -> apply admission controls for resource limits -> select artifact.
- If multiple artifacts are functionally identical, prefer GPU-optimized binary matching customer tier; break ties by artifact publish timestamp (newer preferred).
- When a request supplies force_resolution_token, the runtime verifies token existence & immutability and refuses to run if artifact referenced by token is removed (return 410).
- Fallbacks: if selected artifact is unavailable, try other compatible artifacts within stability_window_days; otherwise follow configured fallback policy (canary->next-tier->error).
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): enable control-plane resolve API + SDK changes behind feature flag for 10% of internal traffic and 2 pilot customers.
Phase 2: default SDK behavior to resolve via control-plane for all new installs; keep legacy local resolver for 30 days behind opt-out.
Phase 3: require rollback_token support in console and expose UI for 'create rollback snapshot'.
Metrics: resolution latency, cache hit rate, rollback usages, broken-pin count, customer errors (409/410).
acceptance_criteria:
- Control-plane resolve API returns rollback_token on every resolution and audits token in event log.
- SDK ModelResolver caches with configurable TTL and honors prefer_short_ttl_for_dev.
- Runtime honors force_resolution_token and returns 410 if the artifact is deleted.
- Compatibility_profile prevents incompatible fallback unless allow_incompatible flag is set and logged.
- PRs for API, SDK, runtime merged and e2e test passing.
- Documentation updated in onboarding guide and Console model page.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: precedence rules (hash>semver>range>tag>latest).
- Integration: end-to-end resolve->generation with rollback_token; deletion of artifact then request with token -> 410.
- Load test: control-plane resolve throughput at target QPS with cache TTLs.
- Chaos: remove selected artifact in runtime and observe fallback respecting stability_window.
- Manual: confirm Console shows resolved artifact and rollback token for pinned rollouts.
migration_notes:
- Existing SDKs will keep local resolution for 30 days; warn on startup when tag-based local resolution is used, include link to migration doc.
- For customers using 'latest' tags, recommend switching to semver-range or create a rollback snapshot before major changes.
- Provide script to batch-generate rollback_tokens for reproducibility in CI.
open_questions: Should rollback_token be globally immutable or TTL-bound? (proposal: immutable until artifact deletion)
What retention window for rollback_token audit logs satisfies compliance customers? (30/90/365 days)
Do we need a signed rollback_token (JWT) to allow stateless verification at runtime? (tradeoff: signing complexity vs. DB lookup latency)
Default stability_window_days: 14 vs 30? Larger windows increase fallback flexibility but may hide regressions.
How should Private deployments mirror rollback_tokens and audit logs? (sync vs. local-only tokens)
tasks: API: add resolve endpoint fields & docs (ENG-17321-api)
Runtime: affinity scoring and token verification (ENG-17321-runtime)
Console: show resolved artifact and 'create rollback snapshot' (ENG-17321-console)
Telemetry: add resolution events and alerting (ENG-17321-telemetry)
